{{Template:optics_dielectric - Tutorial}}

== Task ==

Calculation of the static and frequency dependent dielectric properties of SiC.

== Static dielectric properties ==

=== Density functional perturbation theory ===
Let us start with the calculation of the static dielectric properties.
The most convenient way to determine the Born effective charges, dielectric-,
piezoelectric tensors is by means of density functional perturbation theory
({{TAG|LEPSILON}}=''.TRUE.'').

*{{TAG|INCAR}} (see INCAR.LEPSILON)

 {{TAGBL|ISMEAR}} =  0
 {{TAGBL|SIGMA}}  =  0.01
 {{TAGBL|EDIFF}}  = 1.E-8
    
 ## to get the Born effective charges
 ## and the macroscopic dielectric tensor
 {{TAGBL|LEPSILON}} = .TRUE.
     
 #{{TAGBL|LRPA}} = .TRUE.
 #{{TAGBL|LPEAD}} = .TRUE.
    
 ## to get the ionic contribution
 ## to the macroscopic dielectric tensor
 #{{TAGBL|IBRION}} = 8
    
 ## As an alternative to {{TAGBL|LEPSILON}} = .TRUE.
 ## you might try the following:
 #{{TAGBL|LCALCEPS}} = .TRUE.
    
 ## and:
 #{{TAGBL|IBRION}} = 6
 #{{TAGBL|NFREE}} = 2

*{{TAG|KPOINTS}} (see KPOINTS.8)
<pre>
8x8x8
 0
G
 8 8 8
 0 0 0
</pre>

*{{TAG|POSCAR}}
<pre>
system SiC
4.35
0.5 0.5 0.0
0.0 0.5 0.5
0.5 0.0 0.5
1 1
cart
0.00 0.00 0.00 
0.25 0.25 0.25
</pre>

[[File:Fig dielectric properties SiC 1.png|300px]]

*The {{TAG|LRPA}}-tag
By default the dielectric tensor is calculated in the independent-particle (IP) approximation,
you should see the following lines in the {{TAG|OUTCAR}} file:

 HEAD OF MICROSCOPIC STATIC DIELECTRIC TENSOR (independent particle, excluding Hartree and local field effects)

and
 
 MACROSCOPIC STATIC DIELECTRIC TENSOR (including local field effects in DFT)

which comes later in the {{TAG|OUTCAR}} file.

If one adds

 {{TAG|LRPA}}=.TRUE.

to the {{FILE|INCAR}} above, the second instance will include local field effect
only with respect to the response in the Hartree part of the potential, i.e., in the
''random-phase-approximation'' (RPA).
Search for

 MACROSCOPIC STATIC DIELECTRIC TENSOR (including local field effects in RPA (Hartree))

in the {{FILE|OUTCAR}}.

*The Born effective charge tensors (<math>Z^{*}_{ij}</math>)
Roughly speaking, the Born effective tensors provide a measure of how much charge
effectively moves with an atom when you displace it.
For a definition see the article on [[Berry_phases_and_finite_electric_fields|Berry phases and finite electric fields]].
For {{TAG|LEPSILON}}=.TRUE., the Born effective charge tensors are written near the end of the {{FILE|OUTCAR}} file.

Look for

 BORN EFFECTIVE CHARGES (in e, cummulative output)

'''Mind''': you will find this entry only if {{TAG|LRPA}}=.FALSE. (default), since the Born-effective charges in the RPA tend to be nonsensical.

* The {{TAG|LPEAD}}-tag
As an alternative to solving a linear Sternheimer equation (Eq. 32 of <ref name="gajdos:prb:06"/>), one may
compute <math>| \nabla_{\mathbf{k}} \tilde{u}_{n\mathbf{k}} \rangle</math> from finite differences by specifying

 {{TAG|LPEAD}}=.TRUE.


in the {{FILE|INCAR}} file.
The derivative of the cell-periodic part of the wave function w.r.t. the Bloch vector is then computed
by means of a fourth-order finite difference stencil, in the spirit of Eqs. 96 and 97 of <ref name="nunes:prb:01"/>.
The results of the calculation of static dielectric properties by means of {{TAG|LEPSILON}}=.TRUE.
tend to converge more rapidly w.r.t. '''k'''-point sampling with {{TAG|LPEAD}}=.TRUE.

Rerun the example with

 {{TAGBL|ISMEAR}} =  0
 {{TAGBL|SIGMA}}  =  0.01
 {{TAGBL|EDIFF}}  = 1.E-8
    
 ## to get the Born effective charges
 ## and the macroscopic dielectric tensor
 {{TAGBL|LEPSILON}} = .TRUE.
 {{TAGBL|LPEAD}} = .TRUE.

This will allow for a clean comparison with the next topic.

=== Response to finite electric fields ===
The second way one may compute the static dielectric properties is from [[Berry_phases_and_finite_electric_fields|self-consistent response of the system to a finite electric field]].<ref name="souza:prl:02"/>

*{{TAG|INCAR}}

 {{TAGBL|ISMEAR}} =  0
 {{TAGBL|SIGMA}}  =  0.01
 {{TAGBL|EDIFF}}  = 1.E-8
     
 {{TAGBL|LCALCEPS}} = .TRUE.

=== Ionic contributions to the static dielectric properties ===
To obtain the ionic contributions to the static dielectric properties one needs to compute the force-constant matrices (Hessian of the total energy w.r.t. the ionic positions) and internal strain tensors (second derivative of the total energy w.r.t. strain fields and ionic postions).
These properties may be obtained from finite differences ({{TAG|IBRION}}=5 or 6) or from perturbation theory ({{TAG|IBRION}}=7 or 8).
Try the following

*{{TAG|INCAR}}

 {{TAGBL|ISMEAR}} =  0
 {{TAGBL|SIGMA}}  =  0.01
 {{TAGBL|EDIFF}}  = 1.E-8
    
 ## to get the Born effective charges
 ## and the macroscopic dielectric tensor
 {{TAGBL|LEPSILON}} = .TRUE.
 {{TAGBL|LPEAD}} = .TRUE.
     
 ## to get the ionic contribution
 ## to the macroscopic dielectric tensor
 {{TAGBL|IBRION}} = 8

and search for

 MACROSCOPIC STATIC DIELECTRIC TENSOR IONIC CONTRIBUTION

 ELASTIC MODULI IONIC CONTR (kBar)

 PIEZOELECTRIC TENSOR IONIC CONTR  for field in x, y, z        (C/m^2)

in the {{FILE|OUTCAR}} file.

== Frequency dependent dielectric response ==
Frequency dependent dielectric functions may be computed at various levels of approximation:
# In the independent-particle approximation.
# Including local field effects in the random-phase-approximation.
# Including local field effects in DFT.

Whatever we may choose to do afterwards in terms of dielectric response calculations,
we have to start with a standard DFT (or hybrid functional) calculation

*{{TAG|INCAR}} (see INCAR.DFT)

 {{TAGBL|ISMEAR}} =  0
 {{TAGBL|SIGMA}}  =  0.01
 {{TAGBL|EDIFF}}  = 1.E-8

*{{TAG|KPOINTS}} (see KPOINTS.6)
<pre>
6x6x6
 0
G
 6 6 6
 0 0 0
</pre>

'''Mind''': keep the {{FILE|WAVECAR}} file, you're going to need it in the following.

=== The independent-particle picture ===
To compute the frequency dependent dielectric function in the independent-particle (IP) picture
we restart from the {{FILE|WAVECAR}} of the previous run, with the following {{FILE|INCAR}}
*{{TAG|INCAR}} (see INCAR.LOPTICS)

 {{TAGBL|ALGO}} = Exact
 {{TAGBL|NBANDS}}  = 64
 {{TAGBL|LOPTICS}} = .TRUE. ; {{TAGBL|CSHIFT}} = 0.100
 {{TAGBL|NEDOS}} = 2000
    
 ## and you might try with the following
 #{{TAGBL|LPEAD}} = .TRUE.
    
 {{TAGBL|ISMEAR}} =  0
 {{TAGBL|SIGMA}}  =  0.01
 {{TAGBL|EDIFF}}  = 1.E-8

The frequency dependent dielectric functions is written to the {{FILE|OUTCAR}} file.
Search for

  frequency dependent IMAGINARY DIELECTRIC FUNCTION (independent particle, no local field effects)

and

  frequency dependent      REAL DIELECTRIC FUNCTION (independent particle, no local field effects)

To visualize the real and imaginary parts of the frequency dependent dielectric function you may
use <tt>p4vasp</tt>

 p4v vasprun.xml

or run the following bash-script (<tt>plotoptics2</tt>)
<pre>
awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /imag/,\
                /\/imag/ \
                 {a[i]=$2 ; b[i]=$3 ; i=i+1} \
     END{for (j=12;j<i-3;j++) print a[j],b[j]}' vasprun.xml > imag.dat

awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /real/,\
                /\/real/ \
                 {a[i]=$2 ; b[i]=$3 ; i=i+1} \
     END{for (j=12;j<i-3;j++) print a[j],b[j]}' vasprun.xml > real.dat

cat >plotfile<<!
# set term postscript enhanced eps colour lw 2 "Helvetica" 20
# set output "optics.eps"
plot [0:25] "imag.dat" using (\$1):(\$2) w lp, "real.dat" using (\$1):(\$2) w lp
!

gnuplot -persist plotfile
</pre>

*{{TAG|LPEAD}}-tag
As an alternative to the perturbative expression (Eq. 31 of <ref name="gajdos:prb:06"/>), one may
compute <math>| \nabla_{\mathbf{k}} \tilde{u}_{n\mathbf{k}} \rangle</math> from finite differences by specifying

 {{TAG|LPEAD}}=.TRUE.

in the {{FILE|INCAR}} file.
The derivative of the cell-periodic part of the wave function w.r.t. the Bloch vector is then computed
by means of a fourth-order finite difference stencil, in the spirit of Eqs. 96 and 97 of <ref name="nunes:prb:01"/>.

'''Mind''': keep the {{FILE|WAVECAR}} and {{FILE|WAVEDER}} files, you're going to need them in the following.
You might also want to keep a copy of the {{FILE|vasprun.xml}}.

 cp vasprun.xml vasprun_loptics.xml

=== Including local field effects ===
To determine the frequency dependent dielectric function including local field effects one needs the {{FILE|WAVECAR}} and {{FILE|WAVEDER}} files from the previous calculation ({{TAG|ALGO}}=Exact and {{TAG|LOPTICS}}=.TRUE., and sufficient virtual orbitals), and

*{{TAG|INCAR}} (see INCAR.CHI)
 
 # Frequency dependent dielectric tensor with and
 # without local field effects in RPA
 # N.B.: beware one first has to have done a
 # calculation with {{TAGBL|ALGO}}=Exact, {{TAGBL|LOPTICS}}=.TRUE.
 # and a reasonable number of virtual states (see above)
 {{TAGBL|ALGO}} = CHI
        
 # be sure to take the same number of bands as for
 # the {{TAGBL|LOPTICS}}=.TRUE. calculation, otherwise the
 # WAVEDER file is not read correctly
 {{TAGBL|NBANDS}} = 64
    
 {{TAGBL|ISMEAR}} =  0
 {{TAGBL|SIGMA}}  =  0.01
 {{TAGBL|EDIFF}}  = 1.E-8
      
 {{TAGBL|LWAVE }}= .FALSE.
 {{TAGBL|LCHARG}}= .FALSE.


Information concerning the dielectric function in the independent-particle picture is written after the line

 HEAD OF MICROSCOPIC DIELECTRIC TENSOR (INDEPENDENT PARTICLE)

in the {{FILE|OUTCAR}} file.

Per default, for {{TAG|ALGO}}=''CHI'', local field effects are included at the level of the RPA ({{TAG|LRPA}}=''.TRUE.''), i.e., limited to Hartree contributions only.

See the information after

 INVERSE MACROSCOPIC DIELECTRIC TENSOR (including local field effects in RPA (Hartree))

in the {{FILE|OUTCAR}} file.

To include local field effects beyond the RPA, i.e., contributions from DFT exchange and correlation, one has to specify

 {{TAG|LRPA}}=.FALSE.

in the {{FILE|INCAR}} file.

In this case look at the output after

 INVERSE MACROSCOPIC DIELECTRIC TENSOR (test charge-test charge, local field effects in DFT)

in the {{FILE|OUTCAR}} file.

The following bash-script (<tt>plotchi</tt>) uses ''awk'' to extract the frequency dependent dielectric constant, both
in the independent-particle picture as well as including local field effects (either in DFT or in the RPA) and plots the real and imaginary components using ''gnuplot'':

<pre>
awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /HEAD OF MICRO/,\
                /XI_LOCAL/ \
                 {if ($4=="dielectric") {a[i]=$1 ; b[i]=$2 ; c[i]=$3 ; i=i+1}} \
     END{for (j=1;j<i;j++) print a[j],b[j],c[j]}' OUTCAR > chi0.dat

awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /INVERSE MACRO/,\
                /XI_TO_W/ \
                 {if ($4=="dielectric") {a[i]=$1 ; b[i]=$2 ; c[i]=$3 ; i=i+1}} \
     END{for (j=1;j<i;j++) print a[j],b[j],c[j]}' OUTCAR > chi.dat
cat >plotfile<<!
# set term postscript enhanced eps colour lw 2 "Helvetica" 20
# set output "optics.eps"

plot "chi0.dat" using (\$1):(\$2)  w lp lt -1 lw 2 pt 4 title "chi0 real", \
     "chi0.dat" using (\$1):(-\$3) w lp lt  0 lw 2 pt 4 title "chi0 imag", \
     "chi.dat"  using (\$1):(\$2)  w lp lt  1 lw 2 pt 2 title "chi  real", \
     "chi.dat"  using (\$1):(-\$3) w lp lt  0 lw 2 pt 2 lc 1 title "chi  imag"
!

gnuplot -persist plotfile
</pre>

If you have kept a copy of the {{FILE|vasprun.xml}} of the {{TAG|LOPTICS}}=''.TRUE.'' run (e.g., <tt>vasprun_loptics.xml</tt>), you might execute <tt>plotall</tt> to compare the dielectric functions computed with {{TAG|LOPTICS}}=''.TRUE.'' and {{TAG|ALGO}}=''CHI''.

<pre>
vasprun_LOPTICS=vasprun_loptics.xml
OUTCAR_CHI=OUTCAR

awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /imag/,\
                /\/imag/ \
                 {a[i]=$2 ; b[i]=$3 ; i=i+1} \
     END{for (j=12;j<i-3;j++) print a[j],b[j]}' $vasprun_LOPTICS > imag.dat

awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /real/,\
                /\/real/ \
                 {a[i]=$2 ; b[i]=$3 ; i=i+1} \
     END{for (j=12;j<i-3;j++) print a[j],b[j]}' $vasprun_LOPTICS > real.dat

awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /HEAD OF MICRO/,\
                /XI_LOCAL/ \
                 {if ($4=="dielectric") {a[i]=$1 ; b[i]=$2 ; c[i]=$3 ; i=i+1}} \
     END{for (j=1;j<i;j++) print a[j],b[j],c[j]}' $OUTCAR_CHI > chi0.dat

awk 'BEGIN{i=1} /INVERSE MACRO/,\
                /XI_TO_W/ \
                 {if ($4=="dielectric") {a[i]=$1 ; b[i]=$2 ; c[i]=$3 ; i=i+1}} \
     END{for (j=1;j<i;j++) print a[j],b[j],c[j]}' $OUTCAR_CHI > chi.dat

cat >plotfile<<!
# set term postscript enhanced eps colour lw 2 "Helvetica" 20
# set output "optics.eps"

plot "chi0.dat" using (\$1):(\$2)  w lp lt -1 lw 2 pt 4 title "chi0 real", \
     "chi0.dat" using (\$1):(-\$3) w lp lt  0 lw 2 pt 4 title "chi0 imag", \
     "chi.dat"  using (\$1):(\$2)  w lp lt  1 lw 2 pt 2 title "chi  real", \
     "chi.dat"  using (\$1):(-\$3) w lp lt  0 lw 2 pt 2 lc 1 title "chi  imag", \
     "real.dat"  using (\$1):(\$2) w l lt -1  title "optics  real", \
     "imag.dat"  using (\$1):(-\$2) w l lt  0 lc -1 title "optics  imag"
!

gnuplot -persist plotfile
</pre>

Why are the dielectric functions in independent-particle picture from the {{TAG|LOPTICS}}=''.TRUE.'' and the {{TAG|ALGO}}=''CHI'' calculations different?

Hints:
*What {{TAG|CSHIFT}} is used in the {{TAG|ALGO}}=''CHI'' calculation?

Try redoing the {{TAG|LOPTICS}}=''.TRUE.'' calculation with the same {{TAG|CSHIFT}} as VASP chose for the {{TAG|ALGO}}=''CHI'' calculation (see INCAR.LOPTICS2):

 CSHIFT=0.466

*Redo the {{TAG|ALGO}}=''CHI'' calculation with {{TAG|LSPECTRAL}}=''.FALSE.'' in the {{TAG|ALGO}}=''CHI'' calculation (see INCAR.CHI2).

and compare the dielectric functions again.

*The sample output (using a <math>6\times6\times6</math> mesh for the k points) should look like the following:

[[File:Fig dielectric properties SiC 2.png|600px]]
